name: Mike McCorkle
about:
Mike McCorkle is the founder of Capitol Hill Law and of counsel at the Cadiz Law Firm in Denver. A graduate of Tulane Law in New Orleans, with international study in Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Switzerland, he built a practice initially geared to advising other attorneys on complex questions of law, across a broad range of civil matters.

In recent years his work has focused on counselling nonprofits and political organisations. He has advised campaigns, organisations, public officials, and members of the Electoral College and the Democratic National Committee, and speaks regularly on panels for grassroots political groups in Colorado and beyond.
note:
Biography for Mike McCorkle, written from his professional profile at the Cadiz Law Firm after the curator confirmed the identification. The search returned at least four people of that name — a candidate for office in Kansas, this attorney, the founder of Capitol Hill Law, and several unconnected social accounts — and none of them is linked to NPPC in any public source, so the identification came from the curator rather than from the research.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT. His firm page ends with where he lives and his wife's name. Neither belongs on a staff page, and least of all on the staff page of an organisation whose work is political prosecutions: a home neighbourhood and a spouse's name are exactly the details that should not be volunteered about someone who represents political defendants. Only professional facts are used.

HIS OWN WORDS WOULD BE BETTER. This is assembled from a law-firm profile written for a different purpose, so it describes his commercial practice rather than what he does for NPPC — which is the thing a reader of this page actually wants to know. It should be shown to him before or shortly after it goes up, and replaced with whatever he would rather say.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN FOR BRIAN MULHEARN. He has no public professional footprint that could be found, and inventing one is not an option. His entry keeps its empty biography until he supplies something.
